- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (e.g., first 10–15 days of 30d forecast).
- Forecasts show upward trend bias, particularly after recent price spikes; model fails to correct for mean reversion.
- Overshoots occur after sharp price increases; model lags in recognizing downward momentum.
- Forecast mean is typically 5–10% above true outcome, especially in high-volatility periods.
- Model underreacts to sudden drops in price; fails to anticipate sharp corrections.
- Forecasts exhibit diminishing sensitivity to recent low prices; model overweights recent highs.
- In periods of sustained high prices, model tends to overpredict further increases.
- Model exhibits “sticky” behavior — fails to adjust quickly to new data, especially after price corrections.
- Forecast error is more pronounced in the first 5–7 days of the 30d window; later days show better alignment.
- Model underestimates volatility in late forecast periods, leading to underprediction of sharp reversals.
